messages.content: Vaccines train your immune system to recognize and fight specific diseases without you having to get sick first. They do this by introducing something that looks like the real pathogen - either a weakened/dead version of it, or just a piece of it like a protein. Your immune system responds by creating antibodies and memory cells. Then if you're later exposed to the actual disease, your body recognizes it immediately and can mount a fast, strong defense before you get sick.
